newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexicans against Salinas returning home - PRI leader.
newsitem.headline: Mexicans against Salinas returning home - PRI leader.

text.p: The leader of Mexico's ruling party said the great majority of Mexicans did not want former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari to return home from self-imposed exile in Ireland.
Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) president Humberto Roque Villanueva was reacting to a weekend magazine report that Salinas intended to return to Mexico soon.
"It's very clear to me that the immense majority of people don't want to see him here," Roque told reporters Tuesday. "But that's his problem."
Roque said there was nothing to stop Salinas coming back to Mexico if he so wished. Either way, he added, the PRI would not be affected because it had already distanced itself from him.

The Mexican news weekly Proceso published Sunday a brief interview with Salinas, conducted in Dublin, in which the former president said: "I will soon be in Mexico". Asked if the term "soon" was not vague, Salinas replied "You are mistaken, its meaning is extremely clear."
Salinas was extremely popular during his 1988-1994 presidency but only weeks after he stepped down, the economy collapsed and allegations of massive official corruption began to surface.
Salinas fled Mexico in March 1995, days after his brother Raul was arrested on murder charges, and has not returned since.
The PRI expelled Raul Salinas last year but decided to delay a decision on throwing out Carlos until after crucial July 6 congressional elections.
